transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-22
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Redwood Solutions), Jordan Lee (BrightFind Head of Search), Maya Gupta (BrightFind ML), Evan Ortiz (BrightFind Infra), Sofia Park (BrightFind PM)

Auto Summary: (auto-generated) Deep dive on embeddings reranking perf/cost, lots of numbers and benchmarking requests.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're gonna run through some perf numbers and tradeoffs for embeddings and reranking. Priya's gonna lead on throughput.
00:12 Jordan: Thanks Alex. We are mainly worried about p95 latency under 100ms for reranking of top-50 candidates, and cost — we need to know ballpark cost per query across dims.
00:22 Priya: Got it. quick qualifier — is top-50 full rerank or a two-stage rerank? like recall first with vector db then rerank?
00:28 Jordan: two-stage, yes; vector DB returns top-200 then we embed+rerank top-50 in real-time.
00:36 Priya: ok that helps. typical pattern we see is embedding dim and batch size drive GPU throughput; also KV cache is less relevant for pure embedding lookups but matters if you have generation steps. for reranking we focus on dense vector ops.
00:50 Maya: our current baseline uses 768-dim embeddings, batch size 16 on CPU nodes; p95 is around 420ms and cost is a little high.
:01:03 Priya: 420ms on CPU makes sense. on GPU we can get p95 down to sub-50ms depending on batch and quant. So let's go over dims: 128/256/768/1024 and tradeoffs.
01:18 Samir: quick note — when we say quantization for embeddings we mean running the embedding model with int8 or 4-bit kernels which reduces memory and increases arithmetic throughput; for vectors stored in DB you can also compress but that's separate.
01:32 Evan: for on-prem we have A100s but limited slots; networking to VPCs is a concern — we need to ensure private link with TLS and KMS integration for keys.
01:42 Alex: noted, we'll include KMS/HSM patterns in the security doc.
01:50 Priya: performance numbers, rough: with 768-dim on a single T4 or A10g-like instance, you can expect around 500–1k emb/s depending on batch. p50 might be 10–20ms, p95 grows with load and small batches. with a70/A100 you get much higher throughput. if you quantize to int8 you can often double throughput but you should validate quality.
02:18 Jordan: can you quantify cost per rerank? like per query for top-50 rerank?
02:24 Priya: ballpark calc — embedding cost + rerank compute. Example: 768-dim, running efficient batched dot-product on GPU; if you amortize GPU instance cost, you might be in the 0.3–1.5 cents per rerank range depending on utilization and batch sizing. dedicated pools reduce that. this is rough.
02:45 Maya: that's promising. what about batch sizes? we need sub-100ms p95 for interactive UX.
02:52 Priya: for strict p95 <100ms you often need small batches (1..8) and lower dims (128/256) or faster instance types. there's a throughput/latency curve: big batch sizes (64..512) give excellent tokens/sec/embeddings/sec but increase p95 latency.
03:15 Alex: I'll interrupt — one optimization is asynchronous batching with latency SLOs: you cap batch wait to e.g., 15ms, and if batch not filled you send partial batch to hit latency. that gives good throughput with bounded latency.
03:30 Jordan: does Redwood support that in runtime?
03:33 Priya: yes, our serving runtime has adaptive batching with latency targets; you can set max wait and max batch size per route. it also supports automatic KV cache reuse but again that's more generation than embedding.
03:48 Maya: quality question — how bad is quantization for semantic similarity? we measured small drop with 4-bit in other models.
03:56 Samir: quality delta depends on model. for some open models int8 barely moves nearest neighbor ordering; for others you need 8->4-bit tuning. we recommend running offline evals (MRR/NDCG) on a labeled set.
04:12 Priya: exactly — we'll run dims 128/256/768/1024 with int8 and 4-bit profiles on your sample and compute recall/regression vs baseline.
04:22 Jordan: what about memory for storing vectors? we have 100M items. dims matter a lot.
04:28 Priya: storage cost - 100M * dim * bytes-per-dim. example: float32 768 -> ~300GB; int8 or float16 halves that. DBs offer compression/IVF/HNSW tradeoffs. that's part of cost-per-query too because more compact vectors mean cheaper RAM-backed DB.
04:45 Evan: on-prem, our infra team prefers models pinned to certain GPUs and limited capacity; burst to cloud might be needed. can Redwood support hybrid routing?
04:53 Alex: yes, smart routing allows on-prem primary with fallback to hosted variants in a different region or cheaper endpoints. we can route by policy and region.
05:08 Maya: small nit — can we get sample latency p95 numbers for reranking top-50 at batch sizes 1, 4, 16 for dims 256 and 768?
05:16 Priya: yes that's in the benchmark plan.
05:20 Jordan: also curious about vector db prescoring vs pure GPU rerank cost — sometimes it's cheaper to increase DB recall than run a heavier reranker.
05:28 Samir: true — you want an allocation where DB retrieves good candidates so reranker is small. we can model cost of larger candidate sets vs rerank heaviness.
05:36 Priya: let's talk about batching behavior in the runtime — continuous batching accumulates requests up to a TTL; if throughput is low we default to small batches to meet SLOs. it also supports heterogeneous batches and padding optimizations for transformer models; for embeddings the ops are usually uniform so batching is straightforward.
06:00 Jordan: do you have any recommendations on vector dims for e-commerce search? our queries are short and recall is important.
06:07 Priya: e-comm often benefits from 256..768; 256 is a good tradeoff for latency and recall for shorter queries, 768 improves recall but at cost. run evals to choose.
06:15 Maya: For reranking, we re-score by concatenating some metadata and running a small cross-encoder. does Redwood support collocated runs so embeddings and rerank happen near each other?
06:26 Alex: yes, you can colocate model routes to the same pool and have low-latency calls between them — that reduces egress.
06:34 Evan: KMS integration — we require customer-managed keys for on-prem; is that supported?
06:39 Alex: we support KMS/HSM integrations; on Private you can bring keys and we integrate with audit logs.
06:46 Priya: back to quantization — for inference of embeddings we commonly see these patterns: fp16 gives stability and memory savings; int8 helps on specific kernels; 4-bit aggressive but needs calibration. we'll include per-model recommended profiles.
07:05 Jordan: Ok let's get into concrete benchmark design.
07:09 Priya: plan: we take your 10k sample, run embeddings dims 128/256/768/1024, for each run quant profiles (fp16, int8, 4-bit) where available. For each config run batch sizes [1,4,8,16,32,64], collect p50/p95/p99 and throughput. Also measure rerank top-k costs for k=10,50,100 and compute per-query cost based on Dedicated hourly rate.
07:36 Maya: perfect. can you also log GPU util and memory?
07:39 Priya: yes.
07:41 Samir: we should also run a Dedicated reserved capacity scenario where we estimate 99% utilization vs a bursty hosted scenario to show cost differences.
07:51 Jordan: timeline?
07:53 Alex: Priya said she'd run the first pass by next week. we also need the security docs and pricing.
07:59 Priya: I'll start with a small subset on A10g then scale to A100 for comparison.
08:05 Maya: any gotchas with batching and padding we should watch for?
08:09 Priya: for embeddings less padding problems, but watch memory amplification with big batch sizes; also tail latencies when batch sizes fill unevenly under heterogeneous input lengths.
08:20 Evan: networking for on-prem: do you support private link and VPC endpoints?
08:25 Alex: yes, private link and VPC peering patterns; we'll send the network topology doc.
08:31 Jordan: can you share any public benchmarks?
08:34 Priya: we have reference perf profiles for common open models; I'll share those plus the benchmark harness. expect some variability based on your model.
08:44 Maya: quality regression alerting — do you have tooling to detect embedding drift after quantization?
08:49 Samir: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals — you can hook a reranking eval suite.
08:58 Jordan: about the DB layer, we currently use Milvus. does Redwood integrate with vector stores or do you recommend co-locating approximate nearest neighbor on the same network?
09:09 Priya: we integrate with common vector DBs; colocation helps for latency. we usually recommend RAM-backed index with good sharding.
09:20 Maya: what about caching top candidates to avoid compute on repeated queries?
09:24 Priya: yes, prefix/KV caching helps for repeated queries or session-based reranking; runtime can cache embeddings or reranker outputs depending on TTL.
09:33 Jordan: ok time check — we have about 40 minutes left but this is great.
09:38 Priya: quick example numbers (back-of-envelope): 256-dim, batch=4 on A10g -> p50 ~6ms, p95 ~30ms for embedding; rerank top-50 using a small cross-encoder (quantized) p95 ~40-80ms depending on model. combined you could be under 100ms in optimized path.
10:05 Maya: good. how do you measure end-to-end p95 — do you include DB lookup?
10:10 Priya: we instrument per-stage: DB fetch, embedding compute, rerank compute, network. end-to-end p95 includes all. we provide traces in Console with per-route breakdown.
10:20 Jordan: what's the typical utilization to hit the cheaper per-query numbers?
10:24 Samir: usually you need consistent utilization above 60–70% for reserved pools; otherwise hosted pay-as-you-go can be cheaper for spiky workloads.
10:33 Alex: action items recap: Priya runs benchmarks; Alex sends security & pricing; Maya sends sample.
10:40 Sofia: can we get a deck summarizing tradeoffs for execs?
10:44 Alex: yes, we'll produce a short one-pager summarizing dims vs cost vs latency.
10:48 Jordan: any final risks to call out?
10:51 Priya: quantization risk to quality, network egress for hybrid, and tail latency during cold starts. we'll quantify these in the benchmark.
10:59 Jordan: great thanks. last question — do you support model rollouts and A/B for reranker variants?
11:04 Alex: yes, canary deploys and A/B testing by route and rollout policy.
11:10 Maya: thanks all. we'll send the 10k sample by tomorrow.
11:14 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with benchmark script and schedule.
